Mitigated in code, bump pending the seven-day rule. The advisory (published 2026-10-23) is a DoS in body-parser's inflate path: trailing bytes after a compressed request body. configureBodyParsers (src/common/http-defaults.ts) sets inflate: false on both parsers, so a body with Content-Encoding is refused with 415 before anything decompresses it (src/common/http-defaults.spec.ts proves gzip and deflate never reach a handler). The only patched 2.x release, body-parser 2.4.0, was published 2026-10-22; the repository installs versions at least seven days old, so it is bumped on 2026-10-29 or later. This entry expires before the bump can be forgotten.

No patched release exists: <=1.4.0 is marked vulnerable and 1.4.0 is the newest version (checked 2026-10-06); npm's only suggestion is a major expo upgrade. node-forge is pulled in by expo's development tooling (the dev server and CLI), not imported by the application bundle; the affected RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 verification is never performed on anything the app receives. Re-check the chain with `npm ls node-forge --package-lock-only` before renewing; remove when upstream ships a fix.

A patched release exists only as a new major: the advisory marks <=2.0.2 vulnerable and the fix is 2.0.3+, while metro (the React Native bundler) declares image-size ^1.x and reads its v1 API, so the fix cannot be forced in without breaking the bundle (checked 2026-10-06). image-size only ever parses this repository's own committed image assets at build time — attacker-supplied files never reach it. Remove this entry when metro moves to image-size 2.
Same situation and same surface as GHSA-w3rx-r6r6-pgpr (JXL/HEIF parsers): fixed only in image-size 2.0.3+, outside metro's ^1.x range. Remove when metro moves to image-size 2.

No patched release in the range that can be installed: zod is fixed only in 4.6.6, a new major, and the one package that pulls zod in, @expo/cli (Expo's development and build CLI), declares zod ^3.25.76 in every release up to the newest, 58.1.14 (checked 2026-10-23). The SDK 57 CLI on claude/appbygget does the same. No app code imports zod and the app bundle does not contain it; the CLI validates the developer's own config and command-line input on the developer's machine or in EAS Build, so an attacker-sized collection never reaches it. Remove when @expo/cli moves to zod 4.6.6+; re-check with `npm view @expo/cli@latest dependencies.zod`.
